Author Affiliations: Digital Business, Universitas Negeri Surabaya, Surabaya, Indonesia; Digital Business, Universitas Negeri Surabaya, Surabaya, Indonesia; Digital Business, Universitas Negeri Surabaya, Surabaya, Indonesia; Digital Business, Universitas Negeri Surabaya, Surabaya, Indonesia
Publication Title: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
Abstract: The development of technology and information has changed consumer behavior. Hence, the marketing strategy challenge lies in how effectively it can increase awareness, conversion, and repurchase behavior as the determinants of e-commerce business sustainability. This study explores the influence of digital marketing, brand awareness, and customer relationship management on repurchase intention, with brand trust mediating variables in the e-commerce marketplace. The research analysis tool is SmartPLS 3.0, which shows an influence between digital marketing, customer relationship marketing, and brand trust on repurchase intention. Hence, digital marketing, customer relationship management, and brand awareness must be considered by digital marketers in the e-commerce marketplace to increase repurchase intention. The research is expected to provide managerial implications in the form of contributions to the e-commerce marketplace regarding how effectively digital marketing can reach consumers and inform them about new products, offers, discounts, or promotions that increase conversion rates in the e-commerce marketplace.

Document Title: Improving Digital Project Management Competencies: Case Study of a Digital Marketing Agency in Lithuania
Author Affiliations: School of Economics and Business, Kaunas University of Technology, Kaunas, Lithuania; School of Economics and Business, Kaunas University of Technology, Kaunas, Lithuania
Publication Title: 2023 IEEE European Technology and Engineering Management Summit (E-TEMS)
Abstract: The Covid-19 pandemic accelerated an expansion of digital technologies, with many organizations redefining the skills of their workforce. This paper analyses the case of a digital marketing agency, operating in Lithuania for more than a decade. As the company’s revenue model is based on the execution of successful projects, constant employee competency development is crucial to be resilient and maintain a competitive market position. Thus, this paper aims to determine the core digital project management competencies and propose a competence development plan. To achieve this aim, a scientific literature review and a semi-structured interview with project managers were carried out. The results revealed that the most important digital project management competencies are contextual knowledge, planning and communication skills and ability to adapt to a fast-changing environment. It was recommended to implement the following solutions: form an environment conducive to learning, organize internal knowledge-sharing sessions, promote mentoring/job shadowing, use external coaching services, and provide opportunities for the employees to attend professional conferences and online project management courses. These solutions ought to narrow the gap between the available and required digital project management competencies and help in coping with the challenges of rapid technological progress.
Author Keywords: digital project;digital project management;project management competencies;SME;resilience;Covid19

Abstract: An increasing number of consumers are eager to invest in and benefit from the IoT. Research indicates that by 2020, there will be over 30 billion connected devices, and by 2024, the market for IoT systems is projected to reach $7.6 billion. This paper will focus on the ways in which internet of things (IoT) data could enhance customer relationship management (CRM). An empirical examination was conducted using research methods that utilised qualitative conversations with twelve CRM or innovation marketing experts in 2020 who actually had been engaged with retailer IoT projects. Document Title: Adoption of Artificial Intelligence in Customer Relationship Management: Insights from Bangladesh's Digital Marketing Sector
Authors: M. M. H. Emon; M. A. Rahman; S. Jahan; S. M. S. Noman; Z. Tasnim; J. Mahmud
Author Affiliations: Department of Management Information Systems, American International University, Bangladesh; Department of Business Administration, Uttara University; Department of Business Administration, Daffodil International University; Department of Business Administration, Uttara University; Department of Management, School of Business and Economics, North South University; Department of Business Administration, Uttara University
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Quantum Photonics, Artificial Intelligence & Networking (QPAIN)
Abstract: The main objective of the study is to examine the effect of technological, organizational, and environmental factors, namely, PU of AI, OR, TC, and CP, and their interplay with each other on the adoption of AI-powered CRM in the context of digital marketing in Bangladesh. The quantitative research design was used with primary data being collected by using a structured questionnaire with a 5-point Likert scale. The marketing managers, digital marketing professionals, and CRM specialists were the targeted group and the analysis of 149 valid responses was conducted with the help of Smart PLS 4 and PLSSEM to assess the hypothesis about the existing relationships. The results indicate that all the four determinants have a positive and significant impact on AICRM adoption, with CP having the strongest impact, and then OR, TC, and PU. The findings underscore the interactive effects between technology, organizational and environmental variables in determining the behavior to adopt AI, which justifies the relevance of the TOE framework in a developing country setting. In practice, the study is actionable in helping managers to improve AI adoption through investing in organizational preparation, harmonizing technology systems, and tracking competitor forces. The study highlights socially the prospects of AI adoption to enhance customer experiences and advance more effective digital marketing practices. It is innovative in that it incorporated several determinants in the framework of TOE in the specific case of AI-powered CRM adoption in Bangladesh. The constraints are the convenience sampling and cross-sectional data, which indicates that longitudinal studies should be used in further research.
Author Keywords: AI-powered CRM;digital marketing;AI adoption;TOE framework;organizational readiness;competitive pressure

Publication Title: 2021 IEEE Sciences and Humanities International Research Conference (SHIRCON)
Abstract: Due to the way marketing has evolved over time, creating innovative and powerful messages is insufficient. Today, the companies focus on the communication with each customer in a unique way considering its specific preferences, interests, and individual needs. In this context, a variety of digital signage devices is appearing in the market. This type of product has technologies that are not always fully exploited by their manufacturers and end users. This is the case of the LG Digital Signage devices, which are integrated with a beacon (Bluetooth Low Energy technology-BLE) that is not harnessed by the different content management systems available on the market. On this basis, the research team proposes a content management system which can control the information shown in various LG Digital Signage devices. In addition, to customize the experience, the available beacon in the devices was used to create an interaction between the smartphones of the users and the LG Digital Signage monitor, avoiding direct contact with objects that could be manipulated by others. Consuming the information of an external recommendation engine the necessary information can be obtained. In the experiment, many users were asked to try the system to watch general content as well as the customized one in the available monitors. The effectiveness of the system was also evaluated.
